releases.name: v1.0.3 — bound the blind hold, make the stale cap measure progress
releases.body:
## [1.0.3] - 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- **The inhibitor could be held long after the work was finished.** Two related
  defects let a finished session keep the machine awake:
  - While no plugin instance had a live event stream, `isBusy()` reported busy
    unconditionally and the sweeper refused to drop idle sessions, so the only
    release path left was `staleMs` — up to fifteen minutes with no evidence of
    any work. Reproduced against the desktop app's shared server, where the
    plugin instance is disposed with the workspace and the machine then stayed
    awake until the stale cap expired. The blind hold is now bounded by a new
    `blindMs` option (default 30s, long enough to bridge the stream's own retry
    backoff).
  - A work item whose end event was lost (a dropped stream, a plugin reload
    mid-execution) pinned its session busy for as long as the session stayed
    alive, because unrelated traffic kept refreshing the session's liveness and
    the stale cap — which measured *arrival*, not *progress* — never fired. The
    cap now measures progress, and a finished execution also clears any leftover
    work items, so a turn that ends always releases.

### Changed

- `killInhibitor` now signals through `process.kill(-pid, signal)` instead of
  `ChildProcess.kill(-pid, signal)`. The negative pid targets the inhibitor's
  process group, but the two-argument `ChildProcess.kill` form is not portable
  across the runtimes that can host the server.
- `stop()` re-checks the inhibitor a second later and escalates to `SIGKILL` if
  it outlived `SIGTERM`, so a release can no longer silently fail.

## What changed

### npm description now names "sleep"

The description only said "keeps your computer awake", so the word **sleep** appeared nowhere in the package metadata. That made the package invisible to `npm search opencode sleep` — the most obvious query a user with this problem would type. The description now reads:

> OpenCode v2 plugin that keeps your computer awake and blocks system sleep while any session is generating (macOS caffeinate, Linux systemd-inhibit)

### Repository hardening

- `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-node` are pinned to commit SHAs instead of floating major tags.
- `.github/dependabot.yml` keeps those pins current, ignoring major bumps (action majors change runner requirements and defaults, so they are reviewed by hand).
- `package-lock.json` added so the manifest has a lockfile.
- `.github/SECURITY.md` added with private vulnerability reporting.

## Install

```bash
opencode plugin add opencode-stay-awake
```

Then restart the app, or run `opencode reload`.

## Verification

- 24/24 behavioural checks pass
- `node --check index.js` clean
- `npm pack --dry-run` clean
- CI green

## Fixed

- The README's license badge was a dynamic shields.io npm badge that renders
  "package not found" whenever the registry metadata is cold or is served from a
  cache written before the package existed. Replaced with a static MIT badge, and
  the version badge moved to the `/latest` variant so its URL differs from the
  cached one. Neither can report a missing package now.

## Documentation

- README restructured around time-to-first-success: install, verify and
  disable/remove all sit above the fold instead of several screens down.
- Added a contents list, an ASCII state diagram for the busy model, a
  "why not just use…" comparison against manual `caffeinate` / `pmset` /
  always-on toggles, an FAQ, and a symptom-to-cause troubleshooting table.
- Documented that `opencode plugin add` writes the config key as `"plugins"`
  (plural) while the examples use `"plugin"` — both are accepted and behave
  identically.
- Design notes record the v2 plugin contract, event envelope, the
  de-duplication requirement and the Bun `appendFile` gotcha.

No behavioural change — the plugin code is byte-identical to 1.0.0.

## What it does

Keeps your computer awake while OpenCode is **actually working** — and lets it sleep again the moment every session goes idle.

Long agent runs (model streaming, tool execution, compaction, rate-limit retries) routinely take minutes with no user input. Default OS power settings treat that as idle and suspend mid-prompt. This plugin holds a system sleep inhibitor for exactly the duration of the work, then releases it.

- **macOS** — `caffeinate -dims -w <server pid>`
- **Linux** — `systemd-inhibit --what=sleep:idle`, bound to the server pid
- **Other platforms** — inert no-op

## Install

```bash
opencode plugin add opencode-stay-awake
```

or in `opencode.json`:

```json
{ "plugin": [["opencode-stay-awake", { "graceMs": 5000 }]] }
```

## How it decides "busy"

Deliberately **event-driven**, not polling. Paired session events open and close a per-session work-item counter:

| opens | closes |
| --- | --- |
| `session.execution.started` | `.succeeded` / `.failed` / `.interrupted` |
| `session.step.started` | `.ended` / `.failed` |
| `session.tool.called`, `session.tool.input.started` | `.success` / `.failed`, `.input.ended` |
| `session.text.started` | `.ended` |
| `session.reasoning.started` | `.ended` |
| `session.compaction.started` | `.ended` / `.failed` |
| `session.shell.started` | `.ended` |

A tool call that runs for minutes (a build, a test suite) keeps its work item open, so the inhibitor survives long silences instead of being released mid-run. A quiet period, a grace period and a stale cap guarantee it is always released and can never be held forever by a lost end event.

Every inhibitor is bound to the OpenCode **server pid**, so a crashed or killed server releases it on its own — the machine can never be wedged awake.

## Notable design decisions

- **`session.get()` is not consulted.** On v2 its `outcome` and `time.idle` are only written when an execution settles, so an actively generating session still reports the *previous* run's outcome. Trusting it would drop running sessions mid-flight.
- **Events are de-duplicated by id.** One server process usually hosts several instances of this plugin (one per workspace) and every instance receives every event, so without de-duplication the shared counters would move once per instance instead of once per event.
- **Never throws during `setup()`.** Any unexpected error degrades to a no-op, so a failure can never silently disable sleep protection.

## Requirements

- OpenCode **v2** (2.0.x), including the desktop app
- Zero dependencies, Node >= 18
- MIT licensed
